players.product: ZT Systems AI rack/system integration for AMD next-generation accelerated compute (Helios), plus AI rack metal fabrication, liquid-cooling manifolds, busbars and high-layer PCBs

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $3.46 billion, up 69.7% versus the same period a year ago and at the high end of the outlook; core Sanmina revenue of $2.4 billion grew 17.0% with growth from all end markets, and the ZT Systems business contributed $1.1 billion, at the midpoint of its outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.46 billion, +69.7% YoY; core Sanmina $2.4 billion (+17.0%); ZT Systems $1.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Communication networks, cloud, and AI infrastructure was 62% of revenue, or $2.148 billion, up 173.2% year-over-year; even with ZT Systems excluded, the core Sanmina communication networks and cloud infrastructure end market grew 33%, an acceleration from the roughly 20% year-over-year pace of the prior six to seven quarters, driven by incremental programs and new customers.
quarterly_data.figure: cloud/AI infrastructure end market $2.148 billion (62% of revenue), +173.2% YoY; core ex-ZT +33%

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings in the third quarter were strong with book-to-bill better than 1.1; Sanmina continued to secure more customer orders for the next-generation accelerated compute business in Q3 (after securing orders with both hyperscale and OEM customers last quarter), expanding its overall customer base, while the legacy accelerated compute platform at ZT Systems has gone to zero.

Sanmina's ZT Systems business (the acquisition announced in May 2025 that created its partnership with AMD) is working in very close collaboration with AMD and joint customers to support almost all pre-production activities for the next-generation accelerated compute program; these non-recurring engineering services carry little revenue but a lot of labor charges and drove the non-GAAP operating margin beat to 8.0%, though longer-term margin is still expected in the 6%-7% range.
quarterly_data.figure: non-GAAP operating margin 8.0% (+230 bps YoY); long-term 6%-7%

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 outlook: revenue $3.3 billion-$3.6 billion (core Sanmina $2.5 billion-$2.6 billion, ZT Systems $0.8 billion-$1.0 billion) and non-GAAP operating margin 7.5%-8.0%; the ZT range is below the prior implied guidance entirely because of a few legacy programs, and the new next-generation accelerated compute program is not included in the Q4 outlook due to revenue recognition timing — it is expected to begin contributing revenue in Q1 fiscal 2027 and ramp over time.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $3.3 billion-$3.6 billion; ZT Systems $0.8 billion-$1.0 billion; op margin 7.5%-8.0%

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2026 revenue expected at $14.0 billion-$14.3 billion, with ZT Systems at $4.8 billion-$5.0 billion for the 11 months (inside the $5 billion-$6 billion annualized run rate communicated at the acquisition); management is 'more confident than ever' in $16+ billion revenue in fiscal 2027, with higher revenue growth in the second half of fiscal 2027 continuing into fiscal 2028, driven by strong demand from AI data center customers.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $14.0 billion-$14.3 billion; FY2027 $16+ billion

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity investments: in ZT Systems the focus is incremental power, liquid cooling, test cell capacity and automation for the next generation of accelerated compute; in core Sanmina, metal fabrication capacity for AI system racks (CPS revenue $546 million, up 29.2%), high-technology printed circuit boards (up to 70+ layers) and a new medium-voltage transformer business; Q3 capex was $100.9 million with $135 million expected in Q4; the business is still 'a little bit constrained by component shortages'.
quarterly_data.figure: CPS revenue $546 million (+29.2% YoY); capex $100.9 million (Q4: $135 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Beyond AMD, management confirmed Cerebras as the additional AI platform win in the core Sanmina business (Cerebras announced Sanmina as a contract manufacturer) and said Sanmina now has capabilities that go across multiple platforms very fast; it expects these core-Sanmina cloud and AI infrastructure wins (new customers and additional platforms) to expand in scale in coming quarters, with some built in core Sanmina factories.

Working capital is expected to build as the accelerated compute program ramps into Q4 and the start of fiscal 2027; inventory net of customer advances was $2.2 billion, up 87.2% year-over-year on the ZT Systems acquisition, with liquidity of approximately $4.0 billion and net leverage of 0.29x.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory $2.2 billion (+87.2% YoY); liquidity ~$4.0 billion; net leverage 0.29x

connects_to.relationship: ZT Systems builds AMD next-generation accelerated compute (Helios) racks/systems; pre-production validation with AMD and joint hyperscale/OEM customers

contracts.signal: ZT Systems is working in very close collaboration with AMD and joint customers to support almost all pre-production activities for the next-generation accelerated compute program; orders have been secured with both hyperscale and OEM customers, with more added in Q3; production revenue is expected to begin in Q1 fiscal 2027 and ramp over time through fiscal 2027 into fiscal 2028.
contracts.date_signed: orders secured Q2-Q3 FY2026; revenue from Q1 FY2027

contracts.signal: The ZT Systems partnership with AMD dates from the ZT Systems deal announced in May 2025; the business was expected at a $5 billion-$6 billion annualized run rate in its first year, and AMD 'continues to add more customers', which management says broadens Sanmina's addressable market for AMD Helios production even though share is hard to gauge.
contracts.value: ZT Systems run rate $5 billion-$6 billion (FY2026)
